questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 3 weeks. Inguinal lymph nodes are non-tender and rubbery. Dark-field microscopy of the exudate reveals motile corkscrew-shaped organisms. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.exp: Painless indurated ulcer (chancre) with non-tender rubbery lymphadenopathy is classic primary syphilis. Treponema pallidum is a spirochete visualised on dark-field microscopy as corkscrew motile organisms. Haemophilus ducreyi causes painful soft chancroid; Chlamydia causes LGV; Klebsiella granulomatis causes granuloma inguinale.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a chronic, progressive swelling of the right foot with multiple discharging sinuses. The discharge contains black grains. Biopsy shows broad septate hyphae with chlamydoconidia. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Black grains in discharge with broad septate hyphae on histology indicate eumycetoma caused by Madurella mycetomatis (commonest cause of black-grain eumycetoma). Actinomycetoma produces yellow/white grains with thin bacterial filaments. Chromoblastomycosis shows Medlar (sclerotic) bodies. Sporotrichosis presents as lymphocutaneous nodules without grains.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman on long-term hydroxychloroquine develops a photosensitive rash, discoid plaques over the cheeks, and oral ulcers. ANA titre is 1:640 with anti-dsDNA positivity. Which histopathological feature of the skin biopsy is MOST specific for her diagnosis?
opts: Interface dermatitis with basement membrane thickening
questions.exp: In SLE, skin biopsy shows interface (vacuolar) dermatitis with thickening and degeneration of the basement membrane zone, together with dermal mucin and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate. This is the most specific pattern. Follicular plugging is more characteristic of discoid LE. Leukocytoclastic vasculitis occurs in urticarial vasculitis but is not the defining lesion.

questions.q: A 22-year-old develops tense blisters on the trunk after trivial trauma. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgA deposition at the dermoepidermal junction. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis (LABD) is characterised by linear IgA deposition at the BMZ on DIF. Bullous pemphigoid shows linear IgG + C3. Dermatitis herpetiformis shows granular IgA in dermal papillae. Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita shows IgG at the floor of salt-split skin.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child presents with hypopigmented, anaesthetic patches on the back and bilateral thickened great auricular nerves. Slit-skin smear shows no AFB (BI = 0). Biopsy shows well-formed granulomas with no AFB. Lepromin test is strongly positive. What is the leprosy classification?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) presents with few well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches, thickened peripheral nerve, negative SSS (BI = 0), well-formed epithelioid granulomas, and a strongly positive Lepromin (Mitsuda) reaction indicating strong cell-mediated immunity. BT may have similar features but weaker Lepromin positivity and less well-defined granulomas.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man with a 10-year history of psoriasis develops a solitary erythematous plaque with central ulceration on the dorsum of the right hand. Biopsy reveals full-thickness epidermal dysplasia without dermal invasion. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bowen's disease (SCC in situ) shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia confined above the basement membrane with no dermal invasion. SCC shows frank dermal invasion. Keratoacanthoma has a keratin-filled crater with pushing rather than infiltrative margins. Paget's shows intraepidermal adenocarcinoma cells.

questions.q: A 5-year-old boy presents with honey-crusted erosions around the nose and mouth that started 5 days ago. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in chains. First-line topical therapy is:
questions.exp: Honey-crusted facial lesions in a child represent non-bullous impetigo, caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes. Topical mupirocin 2% is first-line for localised impetigo per IADVL and international guidelines. Fusidic acid is second-line due to emerging resistance. Metronidazole is for anaerobic or rosacea infections.

questions.q: An HIV-positive patient (CD4 = 350 cells/μL) on ART presents with painful grouped vesicles over the T5 dermatome. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. Drug of choice in the Indian setting is:
questions.exp: This is Herpes Zoster. Oral acyclovir 800 mg 5 times/day for 7 days is standard in Indian practice and widely available. Valacyclovir and famciclovir are alternatives with better bioavailability. Foscarnet is reserved for acyclovir-resistant strains (CD4 <50 or clinical non-response).

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with Raynaud's phenomenon, dysphagia, and skin tightening from fingers extending to the forearms. ANA shows a nucleolar pattern. Which antibody is MOST specifically associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis?
questions.exp: Diffuse cutaneous SSc with proximal skin involvement and nucleolar ANA pattern is most specifically associated with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I), which also predicts pulmonary fibrosis. Anti-centromere antibody is associated with limited cutaneous SSc (CREST). Anti-Jo-1 is associated with inflammatory myopathy. Anti-Ro/SSA is associated with Sjögren's and subacute cutaneous LE.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with intensely pruritic grouped papulovesicles on the elbows, knees, and buttocks. DIF of perilesional skin shows granular IgA deposits in the dermal papillae. She has mild steatorrhoea. Treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis presents with intensely itchy grouped vesicles on extensor surfaces with granular IgA in dermal papillae. It is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Dapsone provides rapid, dramatic relief and is drug of choice. A gluten-free diet is long-term management. Prednisolone is not effective.

questions.q: Under Wood's lamp examination, vitiligo patches show which characteristic fluorescence?
questions.exp: Under Wood's lamp (365 nm UV), vitiligo patches fluoresce bright blue-white (chalk-white) due to complete melanin loss allowing UV light to reflect off dermal collagen. Pityriasis versicolor shows golden-yellow fluorescence. Microsporum canis tinea capitis shows blue-green fluorescence. Erythrasma shows coral-red fluorescence (coproporphyrin III produced by Corynebacterium minutissimum).

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing nodule on the lower lip reaching 2 cm over 6 weeks. Histology shows a cup-shaped crateriform architecture filled with keratin, well-differentiated squamous cells, and a pushing (non-infiltrative) border. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma (KA) grows rapidly over weeks, has a characteristic crateriform cup shape filled with a keratin plug, and histology shows well-differentiated squamous cells with glassy cytoplasm and a pushing base. It may spontaneously regress. SCC is more invasive with an infiltrative base. BCC has palisading nuclei and mucin stroma. Merkel cell carcinoma is a neuroendocrine tumour.

questions.q: A patient with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is started on methotrexate. Which set of baseline investigations is MANDATORY before initiating therapy?
opts: CBC, LFTs, RFTs, and chest X-ray
Thyroid function tests and serum iron
questions.exp: Before initiating methotrexate, CBC (detect baseline cytopenias), LFTs (hepatotoxicity risk), RFTs (drug is renally cleared; toxicity increased in renal impairment), and chest X-ray (pulmonary toxicity baseline) are mandatory. Liver biopsy is not done at baseline per current guidelines. PIIINP monitoring has replaced serial liver biopsies in most centres.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child has multiple 2-4 mm umbilicated pearly papules on the face and trunk. The lesions contain cheesy material on expression. Electron microscopy of extracted material would show:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (poxvirus) produces Henderson-Paterson bodies (molluscum bodies) — large eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions seen on light and electron microscopy. Cowdry type A inclusions are seen in herpes simplex/zoster. Donovan bodies are seen in granuloma inguinale. Negri bodies are characteristic of rabies.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden-onset red tender inflamed nodules, fever, and arthralgia. ENL (erythema nodosum leprosum) is diagnosed. Drug of choice in a non-pregnant male patient with recurrent severe ENL is:
questions.exp: Thalidomide is the drug of choice for recurrent/severe ENL (type 2 lepra reaction) in non-pregnant patients via TNF-α inhibition. Prednisolone is used when thalidomide is contraindicated (pregnancy, females of childbearing age). Clofazimine at 300 mg/day has anti-inflammatory properties useful for steroid-dependent ENL. Dapsone does not treat ENL.

questions.q: A newborn presents with large bullae and skin fragility. Blisters arise from minor friction and heal with milia and scarring. Electron microscopy shows cleavage below the lamina densa. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) is caused by COL7A1 mutations (type VII collagen, anchoring fibrils). Blistering occurs below the lamina densa (sub-lamina densa zone). It heals with scarring and milia. EBS blisters within the epidermis (intraepidermal). JEB blisters within the lamina lucida without scarring. Kindler syndrome shows mixed cleavage levels.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with seropositive RA on methotrexate develops a non-tender skin-coloured nodule over the volar forearm. Biopsy shows central fibrinoid necrosis with palisading histiocytes. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Rheumatoid nodules occur over pressure points in seropositive RA. Histology shows central fibrinoid necrosis surrounded by palisading histiocytes. Granuloma annulare also shows palisading but with mucin in the centre (not fibrinoid necrosis) and is not RA-specific. Necrobiosis lipoidica shows horizontal necrobiosis and is associated with diabetes.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman in the third trimester of pregnancy presents with pruritic vesicles on the abdomen. DIF shows C3 ± IgG in a linear band at the BMZ. The neonatal complication to monitor for is:
questions.exp: Pemphigoid gestationis (herpes gestationis) occurs in pregnancy with tense vesicles, linear C3 ± IgG at BMZ, and anti-BP180 antibodies. Maternal IgG crosses the placenta, causing transient neonatal pemphigoid gestationis (blisters/urticaria) in ~10% of neonates, which resolves within weeks. Neonatal pemphigus results from maternal pemphigus vulgaris (anti-desmoglein IgG transfer).

questions.q: A 50-year-old chronic alcoholic presents with symmetrical hyperpigmented, scaly plaques over sun-exposed skin on the neck and dorsal hands, associated with diarrhoea and dementia. The underlying nutritional deficiency is:
questions.exp: Pellagra results from deficiency of niacin (vitamin B3) or its precursor tryptophan. Classic '4 Ds': Dermatitis (photosensitive hyperpigmented plaques, Casal's necklace on the neck), Diarrhoea, Dementia, and Death. Chronic alcoholism, carcinoid syndrome, and isoniazid therapy are common causes.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with recurrent crops of painful oral ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis. Pathergy test is positive. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Behçet's disease is a systemic vasculitis characterised by the classic triad of recurrent oral aphthae, genital ulcers, and uveitis (which can cause blindness). A positive pathergy test (pustule at needlestick site after 48 hours) is highly specific and is part of the ISG diagnostic criteria. Reactive arthritis involves joint, eye, and urethral triad after infection.

questions.q: During a punch biopsy of an erythematous plaque on the back, the hair follicle bulge region (site of epidermal stem cells) is found at the level of the arrector pili muscle insertion. This structure is located within which skin layer?
questions.exp: The hair follicle bulge region containing multipotent epidermal stem cells is located in the outer root sheath at the level of the arrector pili muscle insertion — within the reticular dermis. These stem cells contribute to wound healing and follicular regeneration. The papillary dermis contains the superficial capillary plexus and type III collagen.

questions.q: A 23-year-old woman presents with a painless, large, beefy-red granulomatous ulcer with raised rolled edges on the labia for 2 weeks. Gram stain shows intracellular Donovan bodies within mononuclear cells. Drug of choice is:
questions.exp: Granuloma inguinale (donovanosis) is caused by Klebsiella granulomatis. Donovan bodies are intracellular bacteria in mononuclear cells on Giemsa stain. Doxycycline 100 mg BD for at least 21 days (until lesions heal) is drug of choice per CDC guidelines. Azithromycin 1 g weekly is an alternative. Ceftriaxone treats gonorrhoea; benzathine penicillin treats syphilis.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasia and a rolled border on his nose. Biopsy shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading, artefactual clefting from stroma, and mucin deposition. Most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Nodular BCC is the most common skin cancer. Histology shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, artefactual retraction clefting, and mucin-rich stroma. Clinically: pearly nodule with telangiectasia and rolled border on nose. Trichoepithelioma also has basaloid nests but with horn cysts, calcification, and papillary mesenchymal bodies.

questions.q: A patient develops flagellate hyperpigmented streaks on the back after receiving bleomycin for Hodgkin's lymphoma. The most accepted pathomechanism is:
opts: Direct toxic effect of bleomycin on melanocytes causing melanin incontinence
questions.exp: Bleomycin-induced flagellate hyperpigmentation: the linear/whip-like pattern mirrors areas scratched by the patient. Bleomycin-induced pruritus (from mast cell degranulation) leads to scratching, and resultant post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation creates the flagellate pattern (Koebnerisation). It resolves over months after stopping bleomycin.

questions.q: A 16-year-old presents with comedones, papules, and nodules on the face and trunk. He has been on topical benzoyl peroxide + adapalene for 3 months with inadequate response. The most appropriate next step for moderate-to-severe inflammatory acne is:
opts: Add oral doxycycline 100 mg OD for 3 months
questions.exp: For moderate-to-severe inflammatory acne failing topical combination therapy, oral antibiotics (doxycycline 100 mg OD or minocycline 100 mg OD) are added for 3 months while maintaining a topical retinoid. Isotretinoin is indicated for severe nodulo-cystic acne, acne failing two courses of antibiotics, or scarring acne. Topical clindamycin monotherapy risks antibiotic resistance.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman presents with centrofacial telangiectasia, flushing triggered by spicy food and alcohol, and inflammatory papules on the central face. No comedones are seen. First-line topical treatment is:
questions.exp: Rosacea presents with centrofacial flushing, persistent erythema, telangiectasia, and papulopustules without comedones (absence of comedones differentiates from acne). Triggers include spicy food, alcohol, UV exposure. First-line topical agents are metronidazole 0.75%/1% and azelaic acid 15%. Topical ivermectin 1% is also approved for papulopustular rosacea.

questions.q: A renal-transplant recipient on tacrolimus presents with a rapidly enlarging painful nodule on the forearm. Histology shows tumour cells expressing CK20 in a paranuclear dot pattern, chromogranin, and synaptophysin. The diagnosis is:
opts: Cutaneous metastatic small cell lung carcinoma
Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
questions.exp: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare aggressive primary cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma, more common in immunosuppressed patients. IHC: CK20 paranuclear dot pattern + chromogranin A + synaptophysin. Metastatic small cell lung carcinoma is TTF-1 positive and CK20 negative — the key distinguishing feature.

questions.q: Patch testing shows a +++ reaction at 48 hours to nickel sulphate that increases at 96 hours. The immunological mechanism underlying this reaction is:
questions.exp: Patch testing detects allergic contact dermatitis, a classic Type IV (delayed-type, cell-mediated) hypersensitivity reaction. Sensitisation involves Langerhans cell processing and T-cell priming; elicitation is mediated by CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells, peaks at 48-96 hours. Nickel is the most common contact allergen worldwide.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man with CD4 count of 40 cells/μL presents with painless purplish non-blanching papules and plaques on the palate and lower extremities. Biopsy shows spindle-shaped cells with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated erythrocytes. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) is caused by HHV-8 (KSHV). AIDS-associated KS occurs with CD4 <200 cells/μL and presents as violaceous papules/plaques on skin and mucosa (palate is classic). Histology shows spindle cells, slit-like vessels, and haemosiderin deposits. HIV-associated KS responds to ART initiation; systemic disease requires liposomal doxorubicin or paclitaxel.

questions.q: A 4-year-old presents with >6 café-au-lait macules (each >5 mm), axillary freckling, and a plexiform neurofibroma. His father has the same condition. The mutated tumour suppressor gene is located on:
questions.exp: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (von Recklinghausen disease) is caused by NF1 mutations on chromosome 17q11.2, encoding neurofibromin (a RAS-GAP). Diagnostic criteria include ≥6 CALMs, axillary freckling (Crowe's sign), neurofibromas, Lisch nodules, optic glioma, or first-degree relative with NF1. NF2 gene (Ch 22) causes NF type 2 with bilateral acoustic neuromas.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with palpable purpura on the lower limbs, haematuria, and arthralgias one week after streptococcal pharyngitis. Skin biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA deposits. Most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: IgA vasculitis (HSP) classically follows URTI and presents with the tetrad of palpable purpura (lower limbs), arthralgia, abdominal pain, and renal involvement (haematuria/proteinuria). DIF shows IgA deposits in vessel walls — the diagnostic hallmark. It is the commonest systemic vasculitis in children but also occurs in adults. ANCA-associated vasculitides do not show IgA deposits.
